These probabilities are my prior-based judgments from general knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 structure. I did not run any data or computation.

The main heuristics I applied:
- Edits that matter most involve conv ops on edges feeding the output (edges 3, 4, 5), and effects tend to saturate when other conv paths already exist.
- Removing or weakening an edge hurts less when it is already redundant, so a "none" edit is usually less harmful when the parent has already been disconnected or is weak.
- A conv edit usually helps more when the parent is a weak op (none, skip, pool) than when the parent is already a conv, so most "parent is conv" conditions get low probabilities.
- Consistency across all three datasets and a meaningful margin are both required, which pushes most claims toward low values.
